_comment: Rules by season (Task 229b; docs/simulation.md §2a). data/rules.json is season 1's rules; each change here applies from its season on, merged over the rules before it (objects merge, lists and values replace). id: a lower-case name; season: the first season played under it (2 or later); never announced on its own (Task 265, Tom: upkeep is quiet; an announcement is its own entry in data/decisions.json); reason: the League's reason, in-universe; changes: a partial data/rules.json. Each season's merged rules are checked like data/rules.json. Logged as rule_change at the start of its season.

changes.reason: With its first draft, the League brings in the rookie rule: every side starts a rookie.
The League tidies its off-season: the draft's second round goes by the table, worst first, and a club with room may sign a better free agent in a weaker player's place.
changes._comment: Tom's notes, 2026-10-25 (docs/finances.md): a 20-year-old record-holding keeper went unsigned in season 2's off-season because every roster was full. Season 4's rules run season 3's off-season, so nothing published changes. Measured (margin 8): good free agents left unsigned (better than the median rostered player) about 18 a season to 10; upgrades about 1.3 a season, a pick on the roster sent down to the reserves rather than released; every balance target and the default parity run met, 12 leagues on the edge of two parity targets as the rules before it are.

changes.reason: Clubs draft with the rookie rule in mind, so a rookie's start costs a side its weakest link rather than its star.
changes._comment: Tom, 2026-10-28 (fix B; docs/simulation.md, the draft): in season 3 the Royale's only rookies were both strikers, so the rule benched O. Beaucourt, the league's top scorer. Season 4's rules run season 3's off-season draft, so nothing published changes. Measured (4 leagues x 20 seasons): a rookie keeping the team's best outfielder on the bench 7.8% of team-matches to 4.5%, an 85+ player 11.9% to 5.2%; every balance target met; over 40 seasons a slight tilt to strong sides (most Cups by one club 8.8 to 9.3, target 9; kept, Tom). Stronger (3) cost more parity; the first pick alone barely helped.

changes.reason: The League's scorers credit the assist to the last teammate to move the ball on before the scorer, and none on a free shot.
changes._comment: Tom, 2026-10-28 (docs/simulation.md, assists): only 58% of goals had an assist, as the last player to move the ball on was often the scorer. Only who is credited changes, never a result. Measured (3 leagues x 10 seasons): 79% assisted; the Compass's winner changes in about 4 seasons in 10, still a midfielder; player of the match in about 6% of matches. LATEST's four-assist matches about 2 a season to 4, kept (Tom: still rare).

changes.reason: The Aegis goes to the best defender of the regular season, judged on quells, goals and assists a game, rather than to whoever made the most quells.
changes._comment: Tom, 2026-11-03 (docs/simulation.md, the awards): a defender is more than a busy tackler, and quells' big totals aren't shown any more. Only the award changes, never a result. Season 5, not 4 as first asked: season 4 had begun, and a rule change is logged at its season's start, so every season-4 match after it would have played differently in the record (the live check refused it). The whole list, as lists replace. Measured (3 leagues x 10 seasons): a different winner in 17 seasons in 30; the same winner two seasons running 4 times in 30 either way.
